name: move_pose
description:
Submit a complete pose target through the Supervisor.
Use when: moving the public link6 controlled point to a stated position and orientation. Send one or both arms under targets; an omitted arm is not commanded. Each arm names its two choices as enums -- position_mode (hold_current, absolute, delta) and orientation_mode (hold_current, absolute_quaternion, axis_angle_delta, world_axes) -- and sends that mode's fields beside them in targets.<arm>. absolute takes position_m; delta takes translation_m and position_frame; absolute_quaternion takes orientation_xyzw; world_axes takes approach_world and jaw_line_world; axis_angle_delta takes rotation_axis, rotation_angle_deg and orientation_frame -- rotation_angle_deg is in DEGREES, and no field here takes radians. To hold one half while changing the other, set its mode to hold_current. Label the target free_space, precision or contact_approach by physical intent, not by controller name. speed (optional) is fast, normal or careful, and sets only the pace: the interaction label picks the path at every speed. fast is the default and the speed for ordinary moves, near objects too: the path is picked and checked the same way at every speed. normal (about 0.3 m/s and 60 deg/s at the controlled point) is for moves while holding an object (fast's hard accelerations can make it slip). careful (about 0.1 m/s and 20 deg/s at the controlled point) is for the last 1 to 3 cm of an approach, contact or placing; for that last bit, slow_approaching: true (fast or normal) slows only the final 2 cm of the same move to careful and is preferred over a whole careful move; use it when placing a held object. Slower speeds cost budget: they use more native actions per call, so use them only where they help. These are guidance, not enforced. Instead of speed you may give speed_m_s, any number above 0: the top speed of the controlled point in m/s, with a turn-rate cap of 200 deg/s per m/s (at least 20 deg/s), both reached in 0.25 s; it too sets only the pace. Whatever the speed, each joint's own speed is the real ceiling (at most 4.5 rad/s at fast, 4 with speed_m_s, 2.5 at normal, 1.2 at careful): where a hand move needs large joint turns, or for a high speed_m_s, the arm moves slower than asked, so a fast request may not be reached; a slow one practically always is. motion.speed.planned_peak_linear_m_s says the top speed the planned path reaches. A long straight line is expect_contact: true. A controlled descent is contact_approach, or a planned path, which is usually about as long as the straight line.
Effect: compiles the request once, plans the path from the measured joints and runs it as one action at the chosen speed (fast: each joint at most 4.5 rad/s, accelerating at up to 60 rad/s^2, no Cartesian speed limit; normal, careful and speed_m_s also cap the controlled point's speed along the whole path). At every speed the interaction picks the path: free_space takes a collision-free path planned from the measured joints around what the cameras see now and the other arm as it stands, a held object moving with the hand (a planned route); precision follows the straight line of the controlled point when the complete change is within 50 mm and 15 degrees and the planned route otherwise; contact_approach up to 50 mm/15 degrees follows the straight line, while a larger contact approach takes the planned route to a pre-contact pose, stops there and follows the straight line for the final 40 mm/9.3 degrees. So a precision move past 50 mm or 15 degrees is planned, not straight, at every speed. The one straight line longer than that is expect_contact: true. Where no planned route is available it is a straight line in joint space to one SDK inverse-kinematics solution of the target (up to a half-turn per joint), screened with the SDK collision spheres for this arm's own self-collision and against the other arm; motion.route says which ran (global for a planned route, joint for that line). A straight line that cannot be followed takes the planned route instead, unless expect_contact is true. A straight line is solved with read-only IK every 3 mm or 1.5 degrees, each point from the previous solution, before anything moves. Before anything moves, the whole planned joint path is screened again with the SDK collision spheres for self-collision, against the table top, and both arms together in lockstep (an arm not moved holds still); no objects, finger links or payload in that screen: the cameras' view of them enters the planned route and the contact check below only, and what they cannot see is free space. The whole move is one action: every physics step (4 ms) the arm is driven toward a target that moves evenly between one joint target per native action (40 ms), with a matching velocity, so it does not stop between native actions. While it moves, the motion stops and holds the joints measured at that moment when an arm lags its commanded joints by more than a quarter of a native action's travel (at least 0.012 rad) for 5 physics steps, or its lag keeps growing (above 0.004 rad and up by more than 0.0015 rad per native action, for a native action: pushed back by something) (stop reason tracking, stop.rule bound or growing_error), or advances less than a quarter of the commanded joint motion over 10 physics steps (stop reason progress: blocked or pushing); it never jumps to catch up afterwards. After the last joint target the arm holds it for up to 5 native actions (3 at normal, careful or with slow_approaching) until every joint is within 0.003 rad (0.002 rad) of it and moves slower than 0.05 rad/s. A move needing more than the 250 native actions one trajectory may use, or more than the episode has left, moves the part of its path they cover, ends at rest and is reported as cut short, never as reached: the receipt says not_reached with failure_code controller_timeout and arms.<arm>.motion_progress outcome cut_short with remaining_to_goal_m, and motion.budget_limited gives remaining_m; residuals, pose_error and the pose target the arm then holds are the cut point's. A cut never stops a turn of joint 6 by 90 degrees or more part way: the covered part ends before it, or, when the move starts with one, the move is refused before anything moves (paced_motion_budget with unsplit_span). When the move is meant to push or move an object (or press something), set expect_contact: true; otherwise the guard may stop the arm as soon as it meets resistance (expect_contact keeps the hard tracking stop). expect_contact also plans the move as a contact, whatever its interaction: the straight line the whole way, at any length and speed, never another path. The straight part of a contact_approach or an expect_contact move leaves the fingers free to touch what they sweep through, and the move is refused before anything moves (contact_path_blocked, naming the link) if a link behind the fingers would go into what the cameras see. A precision move inside 50 mm and 15 degrees has no such check, only the screen above. Carrying a held object normally does not need expect_contact; set it only when you use the held object (or the hand) to push, press or insert against something. The guard is only a backup: it infers contact from tracking error alone (no force sensing), so it stops the arm only when it is clearly blocked by something firm; a light or sliding contact usually goes unnoticed, and it cannot tell which part of the arm touched what. Check the next observation yourself for unintended contact.
Returns: status executed once a fast move ran (the receipt status and motion.status say whether the move completed, stopped or covered only part of its path; at normal or careful: partial when it covered only part, stopped when it stopped), action, compiled_pose, receipt, remaining_budget and motion: route (global, joint, line or staged), speed (speed -- custom with speed_m_s -- speed_m_s when given, slow_approaching, the speed caps, planned_peak_linear_m_s and planned_peak_angular_deg_s: the top speed and turn rate the planned path reaches under every cap, joints included), planned_native_actions, duration_s, status (completed, stopped, budget or terminal), knots_planned and knots_executed, stop (reason tracking or progress, arm, knot, physics_step and the measured joint error) when it stopped, settle (settled, native_actions, joint_error_rad, joint_speed_rad_s), per arm final_joint_error_rad, max_tracking_error_rad and final_link6_error against the planned final pose, joint_line_bridges when a straight line crossed an IK hole in joint space, joint6 (per arm, the wrist roll from the measured joints through every planned knot: start_deg, end_deg, min_deg, max_deg, travel_deg and min_limit_margin_deg to its 179.9 degree limit; the two ends alone can hide a swing), expect_contact (whether it was on; a tracking stop on such a move carries stop.note "stopped by the tracking bound despite expect_contact"), speed_segments with slow_approaching (per arm, each speed's first knot, where the slow segment starts and the native actions each spent), ik_warning when the run predates IK-generator recording (recomputed IK may differ from the original run's), and budget_limited (fraction_of_move, needed_native_actions, remaining_m, limited_by) when the budget covered only part of the move; compiled_pose.targets contains the compiled requested target, not a measured arrival. The returned receipt separates refusal, arrival and non-arrival and reports the executor, route and measured residuals; this backend measures no contact force; the next observation carries the current camera images and sensor evidence. A pre-admission error executes no action.
Does not: ask the policy to choose the path beyond the interaction label and expect_contact; avoid obstacles on a straight line; change an exact requested orientation other than by the free_space jaw flip described below; command a gripper; move an omitted arm; infer contact, retention or task success; jump to a target the arm fell behind.
On error: Refused: an empty targets map or an arm outside left and right; an unknown field, a mode without its companion fields or a field of another mode, each naming the field; an approach_world or jaw_line_world that is not three finite numbers or is shorter than 1e-6, or a jaw line within 5 degrees of the approach axis, each naming the field; hold_current for both halves of one arm, a target equal to the measured pose, a rotation_angle_deg outside [-180, 180] or an orientation_xyzw whose norm lies outside [0.98, 1.02], each as invalid_motion_arguments without a field; a target outside the bound action workspace (workspace_bounds) unless the controlled point is already outside it and the target only reduces the violation; the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). Refused before anything moves, with no native action spent: two arms labelled with different interactions (mixed_interactions); a contact_approach beyond 50 mm/15 degrees where the staged approach is unavailable (route_contact_approach_exceeds_local_bound); a point of the path with no admissible IK solution (paced_path_unreachable, with fraction_of_move and the pose) or whose solution jumps to another branch (paced_path_joint_jump); an IK hole inside a straight line is crossed by a straight joint-space line only when that stays within 5 mm of the line and within 10 degrees of its orientation, else the move is refused there (paced_path_wrist_unwind when the wrist would spin between two IK branches, typically at joint 6's half-turn limit: reach the goal by another route); a planned path the collision screen blocks (self_collision, table_collision, or inter_arm_collision: move one arm at a time or keep the arms apart), with fraction_of_move and native_action; a planned route that finds no way: goal_unreachable (no joints reach the target in the collision world), goal_in_collision, goal_below_support (the fingertips would go under the surface seen below the target), start_in_collision, start_outside_limits or path_blocked; a straight part a link behind the fingers would drive into what the cameras see (contact_path_blocked, with limiting_link and penetration_m); a speed other than fast, normal or careful; a speed_m_s that is not a number above 0 or comes with a speed; slow_approaching with speed careful or with speed_m_s at or below 0.1 (it has no effect there); each as invalid_motion_arguments naming the field; planner_failed when the read-only kinematics query fails. position_mode delta without translation_m is refused at targets.<arm>.translation_m; a field belonging to another mode is refused by name. A stopped move (motion.status stopped) reports motion.stop and holds the measured joints; not_reached in the receipt means execution started but the move stopped, was cut short, or ended outside the endpoint acceptance (10 mm, 0.1 rad) without settling; a move that ends inside the acceptance but whose joints did not come to rest (an arm in contact) is reached with failure_code arm_not_settled and the joint error. Use the named reason and fresh evidence rather than repeating the same target blindly. not_reached preserves endpoint and controller evidence independently of official task termination. Read the fresh observation before proposing another action. Numerical inputs follow compute's Use when rule; send every value in this tool's declared units and frame. move_to, rotate_wrist, rotate_pitch and grasp_execute's arm stages run as move_pose's fast trajectory and stop as described above. Before submission the target gets read-only IK by the planner the move uses, in the world a plan would see. Jaw symmetry: the jaws grip the same when turned a half-turn about the approach axis, so with empty jaws (last gripper command open, nothing noted as held) the requested orientation or its half-turn twin is used, whichever is nearer the current wrist, on every interaction and orientation form; while holding something a quaternion or axis-angle request is used as given, so the held object never turns over, and world_axes takes the nearer of the two too, since a jaw line has no sign; exact_orientation: true always uses the request exactly (for example to place an object facing a given way). compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.jaw_symmetry names the choice (requested, twin_nearer_current, held_no_flip or exact) and the receipt's arms.<arm>.motion_progress repeats it. reach_along_request: if the target fails, the farthest solving fraction of the straight path from the current pose, and that pose. Planning-time IK only. When the target does not solve, reach_along_request also carries nearest_reachable_orientation: the smallest turn of the requested orientation (15 to 75 degrees in 15-degree steps, about axes perpendicular to the approach axis) that solves with the nominal jaw centre held, as a pose with approach_world and tilt_from_straight_down_deg, or none_within_sweep; endpoint IK only. compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.observed_clearance (also on move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch): the jaw footprint's lowest point at the target (fingers, plus the held object's localized extent when the jaws hold a named target) minus the highest surface the current depth images show beneath it or within radius_m; negative means that surface is higher; occluded surfaces are unknown; not a collision check. world_axes compiles approach_world (link6 local +X) and jaw_line_world (local +Y) into orientation_xyzw. compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.target_axes_world, on move_pose, move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch, gives the submitted orientation's world approach and jaw-line directions. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.observed_clearance.claim_boundary (move_pose, move_to, rotate_wrist and rotate_pitch) is "From the current depth images and their calibration only; points inside the measured jaws, the held object and the space above them are excluded as robot, other robot links are not; occluded surfaces and object undersides are unknown; points up to the footprint's top within radius_m count; not a collision check or a contact prediction, and the move is submitted unchanged."; compiled_pose.targets.<arm>.reach_along_request.claim_boundary of an unsolved target is "Read-only IK by the planner move_pose uses, from the measured joints, at sampled points of the straight interpolation to the target; reachability is not proven monotone between samples, and no path, collision, payload or arrival claim."; reach_along_request.nearest_reachable_orientation.claim_boundary is "Read-only IK at each candidate endpoint by the planner this move uses, from the measured joints: the requested orientation turned about axes perpendicular to its approach axis, holding the nominal jaw centre; no path, collision, payload or arrival claim, and an orientation outside the sweep may solve.". The previous applied gripper drive target is held, including an intermediate SDK-limited target. Requested close and applied target are separate in current feedback.
The next observation does not repeat this receipt. Native action budgets are fixed offline and cannot be supplied as tool arguments.

targets.description: Sparse per-arm targets. An omitted arm receives no new target and is not commanded.

left.description: The left arm's target. Omit to leave the left arm uncommanded. Null means omitted.

position_mode.description: Choose with its companion fields in the same target: hold_current takes no position fields; absolute REQUIRES position_m; delta REQUIRES translation_m AND position_frame. A mode alone supplies no values.

position_m.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=absolute. [x,y,z] in world metres. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

translation_m.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=delta, together with position_frame. [dx,dy,dz] in metres. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

position_frame.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=delta, together with translation_m. world uses fixed world axes; end_effector uses current controlled-frame axes. Never inferred. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

orientation_mode.description: Choose with its companion fields in the same target: hold_current takes no orientation fields; absolute_quaternion REQUIRES orientation_xyzw; axis_angle_delta REQUIRES rotation_axis AND rotation_angle_deg AND orientation_frame; world_axes REQUIRES approach_world AND jaw_line_world. A mode alone supplies no values.

orientation_xyzw.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion. Unit quaternion [x,y,z,w]. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

rotation_axis.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_angle_deg, orientation_frame. An x, y or z axis in orientation_frame. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

rotation_angle_deg.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_axis, orientation_frame. Signed DEGREES, not radians. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

orientation_frame.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_axis, rotation_angle_deg. world or current end_effector axes. Never inferred. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

approach_world.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=world_axes, together with jaw_line_world. World direction [x,y,z] of the approach axis. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

jaw_line_world.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=world_axes, together with approach_world. World direction [x,y,z] of the jaw line, made perpendicular to approach_world. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

interaction.description: Physical intent, never a controller name. Omitted means free_space. Null means omitted.

right.description: The right arm's target. Omit to leave the right arm uncommanded. Null means omitted.

position_mode.description: Choose with its companion fields in the same target: hold_current takes no position fields; absolute REQUIRES position_m; delta REQUIRES translation_m AND position_frame. A mode alone supplies no values.

position_m.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=absolute. [x,y,z] in world metres. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

translation_m.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=delta, together with position_frame. [dx,dy,dz] in metres. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

position_frame.description: REQUIRED with position_mode=delta, together with translation_m. world uses fixed world axes; end_effector uses current controlled-frame axes. Never inferred. Omit for other position modes. Null means omitted.

orientation_mode.description: Choose with its companion fields in the same target: hold_current takes no orientation fields; absolute_quaternion REQUIRES orientation_xyzw; axis_angle_delta REQUIRES rotation_axis AND rotation_angle_deg AND orientation_frame; world_axes REQUIRES approach_world AND jaw_line_world. A mode alone supplies no values.

orientation_xyzw.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion. Unit quaternion [x,y,z,w]. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

rotation_axis.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_angle_deg, orientation_frame. An x, y or z axis in orientation_frame. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

rotation_angle_deg.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_axis, orientation_frame. Signed DEGREES, not radians. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

orientation_frame.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=axis_angle_delta, together with rotation_axis, rotation_angle_deg. world or current end_effector axes. Never inferred. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

approach_world.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=world_axes, together with jaw_line_world. World direction [x,y,z] of the approach axis. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

jaw_line_world.description: REQUIRED with orientation_mode=world_axes, together with approach_world. World direction [x,y,z] of the jaw line, made perpendicular to approach_world. Omit for other orientation modes. Null means omitted.

interaction.description: Physical intent, never a controller name. Omitted means free_space. Null means omitted.

speed.description: Optional; default fast, the speed for ordinary moves, near objects too. It sets only the pace, never the path. normal: about 0.3 m/s at the controlled point, for moves while holding an object. careful: about 0.1 m/s at the controlled point, for the last 1 to 3 cm of an approach, contact or placing. Slower speeds use more native actions. Leave it out when you give speed_m_s. Null means omitted.

speed_m_s.description: Optional, instead of speed: the top speed of the controlled point in m/s, any number above 0 (turn rate capped at 200 deg/s per m/s, at least 20 deg/s). Each joint's own speed (at most 4 rad/s) stays the ceiling, so a high value may not be reached; motion.speed.planned_peak_linear_m_s says what the plan reaches. Slower speeds use more native actions. Null means omitted.

slow_approaching.description: Optional; default false. true slows only the last 2 cm of each arm's path to the careful speed inside the same move (with speed fast or normal, or speed_m_s above 0.1; refused with careful). Preferred over a whole careful move for the end of an approach, contact or placing. Null means omitted.

expect_contact.description: Optional; default false. Set true when the move is meant to push or move an object (or press something); otherwise the guard may stop it as soon as it meets resistance. The hard tracking stop stays. It follows the straight line the whole way, at any length and speed. Null means omitted.

exact_orientation.description: Optional; default false. true uses the requested orientation exactly, never its half-turn jaw twin nearer the current wrist (for example to place an object facing a given way). Null means omitted.

motion.description: How the one trajectory ran: route, speed (the speed asked for, speed_m_s, slow_approaching, the caps and the planned peak speed on a straight line), planned native actions and duration, status, knots planned and executed, stop (reason, arm, knot, physics step, joint error and bound), settle, per-arm final joint and link6 errors and largest tracking error, speed_segments with slow_approaching, joint-line bridges, joint6 (per arm, the wrist roll's start, end, extremes, travel and limit margin along the planned path), ik_warning, and budget_limited when the budget covered only part of the move (the move is then cut short, not reached).
